mechanism: HBV core/capsid assembly modulators (e.g. vebicorvir, morphothiadin/GLS4, ABI-H2158; also NVR 3-778, bersacapavir, AB-506)
note: Capsid assembly modulators were profiled in HepAD38/HepG2.2.15 cells for potency and in HBV-infected humanized-liver (uPA/SCID) or HBV-mouse models for in-vivo efficacy; the humanized mouse called the on-treatment HBV DNA/RNA response and the absence of antigen/cccDNA effect correctly, while nonclinical toxicology missed the class's hepatotoxicity (AB-506, ABI-H2158).
label: Hep B (capsid modulators)

engagement.note: NVR 3-778, unlike entecavir, lowered serum HBV RNA in HBV-infected humanized mice: the capsid-engagement signature CAMs were expected to show in patients.
engagement.short: Mice: HBV RNA falls, unlike entecavir
engagement.quote: NVR3-778 and peg-IFN, but not entecavir, also reduced serum level of HBV RNA.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level only (gastrojournal.org full text returned HTTP 403). Serum HBV RNA, which falls when pgRNA encapsidation is blocked, is the only CAM-specific engagement read-out available in patients, so it is treated as the model's engagement prediction.

engagement.note: Sponsor's preclinical paper states the mouse HBV DNA/RNA pattern, including the pegIFN combination effect, translated to patients in the NVR 3-778 phase 1b trial.
engagement.short: HBV RNA signature translated to patients
engagement.quote: This result translated to clinical observations in HBV-infected patients in which the greatest antiviral effect was observed when NVR 3-778 was combined with pegIFN than when NVR 3-778 monotherapy was used.
engagement.reason: Mouse HBV RNA signature seen in patients
engagement.judgement: Same source and sentence as the efficacy cell: Lam's comparison covers serum HBV DNA and HBV RNA together and no source isolates HBV RNA as an engagement read-out. Patient HBV RNA fell 1.42 log10 at >=1200 mg/day (Yuen 2019, abstract only). Medium confidence: the comparison is the sponsor's own and qualitative; print year 2019 inferred from AAC vol 63 issue 1 (online 2018-10-29).

dose.model: HepG2.2.15 EC50 x10 as plasma-trough target, confirmed in humanized mice
dose.note: Trough target >=10x EC50 (~3 uM) was met in humanized mice, which all responded; patient confirmation is cited only as unpublished data.
dose.short: Trough >=10x EC50 target confirmed in mice
dose.quote: This target was confirmed in humanized mice, where all mice showed plasma trough concentrations of at least 3 µM and all mice responded to NVR 3-778 treatment with significant reductions in HBV DNA and secreted HBV RNA levels.
dose.judgement: Lam says the clinical programme moved to twice-daily dosing to reach the target but cites only unpublished data; the patient paper (Yuen 2019, Gastroenterology) could not be read (HTTP 403), so no published patient-side exposure comparison for NVR 3-778 was found. Humanized-mouse troughs (28-31 uM) were ~10x the target.

dose.model: HepAD38 cell-culture EC90 as steady-state Cmin target
dose.note: GLS4/ritonavir was dosed to hold Cmin above the in-vitro EC90; patients reached 3.7-3.9x EC90 and HBV DNA fell 1.4-2.1 log10 in 28 days.
dose.quote: The mean Ctrough of GLS4 was 205-218 ng/mL, which was approximately 3.7-3.9 times the 90% effective concentration (55.8 ng/mL), with a lower accumulation (accumulation rate, 1.1-2.0).
dose.reason: Cell EC90 target met; activity followed
dose.judgement: Call: the exposure target was a floor (Cmin >= EC90) and was met, with dose-related antiviral activity (-1.42 and -2.13 log10 HBV DNA), so scored as matched even though entecavir gave -3.5 log10 in the same trial. The source never grades the prediction; 'match' reflects its framing (target reached, activity observed). My own Hill-1 arithmetic (33-49x EC50 -> 97-98% inhibition) puts the observed declines within 2x of expectation, but that is not from the source, hence magnitude direction_only. The model is a different cell line/drug from the 2019 opener (both are HBV-replicating hepatoma-line EC targets).

efficacy.note: GLS4, the first CAM to reach patients, was profiled in HepAD38 cells and in viremic nude mice carrying HepAD38 tumours.
efficacy.short: GLS4 suppresses HBV in xenograft mice
efficacy.quote: Treatment of mice with GLS4 and BAY 41-4109 showed strong and sustained suppression of virus DNA to about the same extents both during and after treatment.
efficacy.judgement: Opener uses a different in-vivo model from the later entries; included because the class's first clinical compound relied on it. Earlier HBV-transgenic-mouse work on the HAP BAY 41-4109 (Deres 2003) was not verified in this session and is not used.

efficacy.note: Six weeks of NVR 3-778 cut serum HBV DNA and RNA; HBsAg/HBeAg moved only with pegIFN and cccDNA did not change.
efficacy.short: Humanized mice: DNA/RNA fall, antigens don't
efficacy.quote: NVR3-778 has high antiviral activity in mice with humanized livers and stable HBV infection, reducing levels of serum HBV DNA and HBV RNA.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract only (full text HTTP 403). The abstract also states HBsAg/HBeAg fell only in peg-IFN groups and cccDNA did not differ between groups, i.e. the mouse predicted no antigen or cccDNA effect from the CAM alone.

efficacy.note: pegIFN combination beat monotherapy in mice and in the phase 1b trial (1.97 vs 1.43 log10 HBV DNA); HBsAg unchanged in both.
efficacy.short: Mouse regimen ranking held in patients
efficacy.quote: This result translated to clinical observations in HBV-infected patients in which the greatest antiviral effect was observed when NVR 3-778 was combined with pegIFN than when NVR 3-778 monotherapy was used.
efficacy.reason: pegIFN combination effect reproduced in patients
efficacy.judgement: Direction only: combination-treated mice went below quantification while patients fell ~2 log10; in mice NVR 3-778 alone matched entecavir, in patients 600 mg BID gave 1.43 log10 in 4 weeks (entecavir gave 3.5 log10 in the 2021 GLS4 trial), an over-prediction the source does not discuss. Not 'contra' because the best in-vivo model also called the antigen/cccDNA non-response correctly, which the clinic later confirmed (no HBsAg/HBeAg change with vebicorvir, Sulkowski 2022 and Yuen 2022; no functional cure off treatment, Yuen 2024 JHEP Rep). The cell-culture secondary-MoA claim (block of cccDNA formation, Huang 2020) did not translate: Yuen 2024 notes vebicorvir troughs exceeded the protein-adjusted EC50 for cccDNA formation yet no functional cure followed, but that is a different model from the one scored here.

safety.model: HepAD38-xenograft nude mice; primary human hepatocytes
safety.note: First in vivo safety read for a clinical CAM: ALT and body weight normal in GLS4-treated HepAD38-xenograft mice.
safety.judgement: Formal toxicology-species packages for the class are first documented later (Lam 2019: 'favorable pharmacokinetics and safety in animal species'; Huang 2020); this opener is the earliest in-vivo safety observation found for a CAM that reached patients.

safety.model: Nonclinical toxicology panel (rat, dog, monkey PK species; tox data not shown)
safety.note: Sponsor's preclinical paper pairs a clean toxicology panel (data not shown) with vebicorvir's tolerability in phase 1/2a.
safety.short: Tox clean; vebicorvir tolerated in clinic
safety.quote: Finally, ABI-H0731 exhibited no specific target organ or dose-limiting toxicities in an extensive panel of toxicology studies (data not shown) and has also been well tolerated in human clinical studies.
safety.judgement: Toxicology data are 'data not shown' and the comparison sentence is the sponsor's. Vebicorvir's long-term extension later listed ALT elevations as the commonest AE but no patient met flare criteria (Yuen 2024).

safety.model: Nonclinical toxicology package (species not named in the source)
safety.note: AB-506: grade-4 ALT flares in 4 CHB patients and 2 healthy subjects; the nonclinical toxicology package had shown nothing; programme terminated.
safety.quote: to rule out the possibility of drug-related hepatotoxicity, despite no evidence of transaminase elevations or notable liver pathology in the supporting nonclinical toxicology package
safety.judgement: Quote is a verbatim 24-word clause of a 44-word sentence (full sentence exceeds the 40-word cap). The paper attributes the flares to drug hepatotoxicity ('suggesting that AB-506 hepatotoxicity contributed to the ALT elevations') and records the programme's termination; it also notes ABI-H2158's phase-2 discontinuation for hepatotoxicity (press release), so this is a class signal (ALT flares also seen with GLS4 and JNJ-6379 but confounded by host flares). 'contra' overrides the 2020 match per the rules.
